coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Chase Center
record.summary: An 18,064-to-19,500-seat arena for the Golden State Warriors (NBA) and Golden State Valkyries (WNBA, since 2025), anchoring an 11-acre, privately financed mixed-use development in Mission Bay with 580,000 sq ft of office/lab space (leased in full by Uber as its San Francisco headquarters since 2022), 100,000 sq ft of retail ("Thrive City") and a 35,000 sq ft public plaza; designed by MANICA Architecture with Gensler (interiors), built by a Mortenson/Clark Construction joint venture, and opened September 6, 2019.

facts.value: Golden State Warriors ownership (privately financed, no public funds)
MANICA Architecture (design architect); Kendall/Heaton Associates (architect of record)
Mortenson Construction and Clark Construction Group, joint venture
SWA Group (designed the 35,000 sq ft public plaza)
~900,000 total (arena plus 580,000 sf office/lab and 100,000 sf retail)
NBA/WNBA arena (Warriors, Valkyries) plus mixed-use office/lab, retail ("Thrive City"), a public plaza and ~950 parking spaces
LEED Gold (Building Design and Construction: New Construction), achieved about a year after opening; also GBAC STAR facility accreditation
100% renewable electricity via CleanPowerSF's SuperGreen program

Uber occupies the entire office component (Mission Bay 3 & 4 towers, 1655 & 1725 3rd St) as its San Francisco/global headquarters: ~584,000-586,000 sq ft, 20-year lease, ~4,000 employees, 145 dedicated parking spaces
Named under a naming-rights deal with JPMorgan Chase
Golden State Warriors (NBA, since 2019) and Golden State Valkyries (WNBA, since 2025)

open_questions: Chase Center's final cost is genuinely disputed in reporting: $1.4B is the most-repeated figure (Construction Dive), but a Warriors executive (Rick Welts, per Wikipedia) put the actual final cost closer to $1.3B after a roughly 30% overrun from an original budget. A separate 2019 Construction Dive piece on the (distinct, unbuilt) hotel/condo proposal used '$1.5B Chase Center' in its own headline, which appears to conflate the arena with that proposal; that figure is not used here.
Uber's exact current headcount or lease status as of 2026 was not independently verified; the source describing its 584,000-586,000 sq ft lease is from January 2022.

The Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex on adjacent Blocks 29-30 is financially and physically tied to Chase Center but may sit on a separate parcel; whether it falls within blklot 8722025 or is a distinct, not-yet-built record is not confirmed. Current 2026 construction status is also unconfirmed.

No primary Port of San Francisco or OCII page dedicated specifically to Chase Center was found (as a privately financed project, it may not have one); the only agency-level source found was SFPUC/CleanPowerSF's sustainability write-up.
No openly licensed image was found; recommend linking rather than hosting until one is confirmed.

record.notes: Chase Center, 1 Warriors Way (Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32) -- an 18,064-to-19,500-seat arena (home of the Golden State Warriors and Valkyries), anchoring an 11-acre mixed-use development with 580,000 sq ft of office/lab space, 100,000 sq ft of retail (Thrive City), a 35,000 sq ft public plaza and ~950 parking spaces; designed by MANICA Architecture (interiors by Gensler), privately financed (~$1.4B) by Warriors ownership. Opened Sept 6, 2019. Promoted here from an orientation-only landmark (data/landmarks.csv) to a tracked record now that Mission Bay is a real site, per docs/briefs/mission-bay-geometry.md -- the landmark row had pointed at blklot 8722001, a now-retired/superseded parcel; this row uses the parcel's real, active blklot 8722025 (address '7 Warriors Way' in DataSF's own roll). Oracle Park remains a landmark; it belongs to Mission Rock/the Giants, not Mission Bay.
